name: Furl Scornbrow
summary: At a watchtower northwest of Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow keeps watch over Durotar. Too old for the front lines, he crafts sturdy packs for young travelers.

sections.title: Watchman of the Ridge
sections.body: Furl Scornbrow watches the central plains from a wooden tower northwest of Razor Hill. In the tense days after Orgrimmar was founded, sentries like Furl sounded signal horns against hostile quilboar, centaur, and Kul Tiras interlopers. Durotar has since grown more stable, and Razor Hill has secured its borders. Emergencies come less often, leaving Furl long quiet hours at his post.

sections.title: A Useful Pair of Hands
sections.body: Furl says his old bones and fading strength leave him unable to fight. Still, an orc does not easily surrender their purpose. He uses his hands to make canvas sacks and packs for fresh recruits carrying supplies. In exchange for coarse thread and practical materials, he equips green adventurers setting out to prove their worth to the Horde.

faq.answer: Furl Scornbrow keeps watch from a lookout tower atop the bluffs northwest of Razor Hill. Too old for the front lines, he watches for danger and makes bags for young travelers.

faq.q: What is Furl's role in Durotar?
faq.answer: Furl mans the signal horn tower and watches for invaders approaching Razor Hill. With Durotar more secure under Horde control, he sounds the alarm less often and spends quiet hours helping recruits organize their gear.

faq.q: Why does Furl ask travelers for materials?
faq.answer: Furl asks travelers for materials because he believes every member of the Horde must carry their weight. Unable to fight, he stitches practical travel packs for newer warriors and asks only for basics such as coarse thread.

angles.text: Furl shows the orcish belief that age need not end a warrior’s service. Though he has lost his martial strength, he continues to serve the Horde with honor.
Furl’s watch along the ridges outside Razor Hill reflects the vigilance needed to protect Durotar’s young settlements from lingering threats.
